policy: AGENTS.md, documents/agents/orchestrator-policy.md, documents/agents/component-first.md, documents/lessons.md, documents/rounds/README.md, .github/merge-policy.md, and every markdown file in the canonical orchestrator skill (~/.agents/skills/orchestrator/) are review-gated: a change is reviewed by deepseek-v4-pro build 0813 first (cline-pass/cline-pass/mimo-v2.6-pro is admissible in the 12:00–18:00 local window OR when no provider answers with 0813, with the basis stated in fallbackReason), judged against the reason recorded here, which names what changes, why now, and what was rejected. tests/meta/protected-doc-review.test.ts recomputes each sha256 (CRLF to LF, trailing whitespace trimmed, leading BOM dropped) and fails when the text moved after review, the reviewer is not the first choice, a fallback lacks a reason, an entry is orphaned, or a protected file is missing.

reviews.reason: changes: two owner instructions of 2026-11-16 put the implementer and a review at every tier. First, "enforce worker model for all tiers": the worker seat implements at Tier 0-1 as well as Tier 2. Second, "Tier 0 must review also with worker model": at Tier 0 the worker-model seat also reviews the change in a separate session, the parent answers each finding (answered, not necessarily fixed) and the commit body names each finding and its answer, and the parent still self-accepts. Section 3 of AGENTS.md and the tier list, seats table, spec-review parenthetical, "A worker at every tier" paragraph and reviewer paragraph of this file all said the opposite - the parent implements at Tier 0-1 and only Tier 2+ has a worker - so each now states the new rule. AGENTS.md section 17's worker-seat bullet loses its "Tier 2+" qualifier and reads "does not author the implementation at any tier"; the grill-me seat row is relabelled "every round that opens one" to match section 2. why: the superseded wording appeared in six places, and the sentence a worker reads before it starts is the one that had to agree; leaving any of them would make the policy contradict the next round it authorised. rejected: keeping a Tier 0-1 parent-implement exception with a note (the owner asked for every tier, not a larger exception); letting the worker-model review replace the pro seat at Tier 0 (the owner kept protected documents on the section 10a pro-seat review, so a protected Tier 0 change gets both seats); restating the model ids in a new section instead of the existing seats table (one ranking, one source); deleting the superseded sentences (this repo keeps the change visible); tightening "every round that opens one" to "when a grill opens" (the reviewer called it accurate and the churn bought nothing).
reviews.verdict: REWORK then PASS; final text PASS
reviews.attestation: The pro seat (ollama-cloud/deepseek-v4-pro:0813, outside the 12:00-18:00 window) read the first change, approved it, and raised two P1s outside the diff: AGENTS.md section 17 still called the worker "the Tier 2+ implementer" and still said the parent does not author the implementation "at Tier 2+". Both were fixed and re-read, and the pro seat approved the text. The owner then added the Tier 0 review duty. A worker-model pass (ollama-cloud/deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017) - the duty this change creates, run on the change itself - raised four findings: "the reply names them" named no artefact (the commit body now names each finding and its answer); the reviewer paragraph said "in every tier" while the new text says a solo round has no independent reviewer (now "wherever a tier has an independent review", with an explicit Tier 0 carve-out naming the section 10a exception); the seats row labelled the worker "implementer, every tier" without the review duty; and "writes the round doc and accepts" ignored that a Tier 0 record is the commit body. All four were applied, and the pass re-read the files and confirmed each APPLIED, raising one residual P3 on the reviewer row label, also applied. The pro seat then raised two reader risks, both applied: "answered" could be read as "fixed", and the text never said the Tier 0 review is a separate session from the implementer. A final pass over the frozen text approved it and confirmed the Tier 0 duty is implement-where-there-is-code, a separate-session review, the parent answering each finding, then self-accept - not an independent gate and not a replacement for Tier 1 or Tier 2. The parent computed the hashes from that frozen text.

reviews.reason: changes: the "Fluent first" bullet in section 6 gains the owner rule of 2026-11-13 - "Fluent before rewrite: when Fluent provides the control, start from it and shape it through its props, slots, variants and makeStyles", with a bespoke re-implementation of a control Fluent provides being the same defect as a raw element, and the round doc naming the Fluent component attempted and why it was rejected. why: the policy file is where a reviewer looks for the component rules, and a rule that lives only in AGENTS.md would leave this file silently behind the non-negotiable it defers to; the first wording said "native", which in this repo means raw HTML, and was corrected in both files in the same cycle so the two cannot disagree. rejected: restating the exemplars, the mock carve-out and the "at every level" phrase here (they stay in AGENTS.md section 16, which this bullet names as the non-negotiable); a second policy paragraph (one clause keeps the file a pointer, not a rival source). The two owner-gated strengthenings were answered "all as recommended" and are in this text rather than left open: a rejected rewrite must cite a documented gap with its link or a reproducible blocker (awkwardness is not a limitation, and appearance belongs in props, slots and tokens), and a hand-built control where Fluent provides one is a blocking (P1) review finding, not a taste note. A third review round accepted both: P1 is already this repository's word for a blocking finding (the reviewer contract's "P1 (must fix)", and the merge policy's "resolves every P1 before the PR"), so the rule borrows the established severity rather than minting one.

Round one returned REWORK on four P1s (the milestone scope contradicted section 9 and the merge policy glossary; auto-signed redefined `signed` against the policy and the skill; the re-run budget said one and two in adjacent sentences; the hard-gate wording dropped the round-name requirement) and three P2s; all seven were fixed and round two returned PASS.
